title: India Women Script History With 270-Run Victory in First-Ever Women's Test at Lord's
excerpt: Yastika Bhatia scores first women's Test century at Lord's, Kranti Gaud etches name on honours board with five-wicket haul as India dominate England in a landmark four-day match.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India won the first-ever women's Test at Lord's by 270 runs — their biggest overseas Test victory
  • Yastika Bhatia became the first woman to score a Test century at Lord's (113 runs)
  • Kranti Gaud became the first woman on Lord's honours board with a five-wicket haul (5/37)
  • Sachin Tendulkar attended the historic match and praised the team's achievement
  • Captain Harmanpreet Kaur called for more women's Test matches at the iconic venue
India's women's cricket team wrote a defining chapter in the sport's history on July 13, clinching a commanding 270-run victory over England in the first-ever women's Test match played at Lord's Cricket Ground. The result — India's biggest overseas Test triumph — unfolded across four days of dominant cricket that produced multiple historic firsts. ## A Test of Firsts The match, played from July 10-13 at the Home of Cricket, was 142 years in the making. Women's cricket had never graced Lord's in the Test format before, and India ensured the occasion was marked with performances that will live on the ground's storied honours boards. Wicketkeeper-batter Yastika Bhatia stole the spotlight with a magnificent 113, becoming the first woman to score a Test century at Lord's. Her innings, reached with a single to cover off her 145th ball, anchored India's second-innings declaration at 341 for seven and set England a record target of 457. Fast bowler Kranti Gaud produced figures of 5 for 37 in England's first innings, making her the first woman to feature on Lord's honours board for a five-wicket haul. Across both innings, she finished with match figures of 7 for 91 and took the Player of the Match award. ## A Statement of Dominance India laid the foundation with 285 in their first innings, bolstered by contributions from Smriti Mandhana, captain Harmanpreet Kaur and all-rounder Deepti Sharma. They then bowled England out for 170, with Gaud's first-innings demolition of the top order setting the tone from the fourth over. On the final morning, it took just 95 minutes to wrap up the match. Off-spinner Sneh Rana claimed four wickets in England's second innings, bowling Sophie Ecclestone for 50 to seal the historic win as England were dismissed for 186. ## Tendulkar Witnesses History Legendary batter Sachin Tendulkar was present at Lord's to witness the occasion. "Every cricketer carries the dream of playing at Lord's. Over the past four days, a new generation lived that dream as women's Test cricket arrived at the Home of Cricket for the very first time," he wrote on social media. "Smriti's composure, Yastika's brilliant century and Kranti's five-wicket haul made this occasion even more special," Tendulkar added. ## What It Means for the Diaspora For the global Indian community, the victory carries significance beyond the scorecard. Indian women's cricket has long fought for recognition, and winning the inaugural women's Test at the world's most iconic cricket venue cements the team's growing stature on the international stage. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur made a pointed call for more opportunities. "God is a better writer, and he has written it pretty well. Playing at Lord's is always special. Hopefully, we will get 10 more Test matches, and we can keep performing," she said after the match. Kranti Gaud captured the feeling succinctly: "If I had to describe this win in one word, it would be dream." For Indian fans watching from living rooms in New Jersey, pubs in London and cricket clubs in Sydney, it was a dream shared.
